'''Nissan ben Avraham Deliatitz''' ({{Langx|he|ניסן בן אברהם דעליאטיץ}}) was a 19th-century [[Russian Empire|Russian]] [[rabbi]] and [[mathematician]].

He wrote ''Keneh Ḥokhmah'', a manual of [[algebra]] in five parts, published in [[Vilnius|Vilna]] and [[Grodno]] in 1829.<ref>{{cite book|title=Ḳeneh ḥokhmah: ḳolel ḥamishah sheʻarim be-hokhmat algebra|first=Nisan|last=Deliatitz|location=Vilna and Grodno|year=1829|publisher=Menaḥem Man ben Barukh and Śimḥah Zimel ben Menaḥem Naḥum|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/011627143|oclc=19154733|language=Hebrew}}</ref> The work received [[Haskama|approbations]] from Rabbi David, the ''[[av beit din]]'' of [[Navahrudak|Novhardok]], and Rabbi Avraham Abele ben Avraham Shlomo Poswoler, an eminent scholar who headed the Vilna ''[[Beth din|beit din]]''.<ref>{{cite book|title=Untold Tales of the Hasidim: Crisis & Discontent in the History of Hasidism|first=David|last=Assaf|translator-first=Dena|translator-last=Ordan|location=Waltham|publisher=Brandeis University Press|year=2010|isbn=978-1-58465-861-0|page=241|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8o_OePVEXgYC}}</ref>
